title: [Support for Python 3.10] MCMC example in documentation does not work: `AttributeError: __enter__`
author: ayaka14732

comments.author: fehiepsi
comments.body: Hi @ayaka14732, I just tested the code in colab and it is working fine. Maybe this issue is specific to Python 3.10?

comments.author: ayaka14732
comments.body: Thanks! I tested it on Python 3.8 and it works now.

comments.author: dme65
comments.body: Hi @fehiepsi, Looks like this issue is also affecting some of our Ax users: https://github.com/facebook/Ax/issues/893. Are there any plans to look into this issue and have Pyro support Python 3.10? Thanks!

comments.author: fehiepsi
comments.body: @dme65 Could you ping me when PyTorch [supports python 3.10](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/66424)? I will try to fix the issue then. Thanks!

comments.author: nabriis
comments.body:
For me on windows pytorch now installs through conda in python 3.10 @fehiepsi!

I could not for the life of me figure out why after installing pytorch using the default conda install and then pyro from pip I was getting this error. I guess pyro does not check the python version when installing through pip.

comments.author: fehiepsi
comments.body:
> pyro does not check the python version when installing through pip

That's right. This might be an Pyro issue, not an PyTorch issue. Looking at the code, it is not clear to me why the error happens. Hopefully the issue will be resolved after PyTorch officially supports Python 3.10. (I think they set the milestone PyTorch 1.12.0, which is the next release, for it.)

comments.author: fritzo
comments.body:
@nabriis that sounds rough! 😬 

This is a PyTorch issue. I believe all of Pyro is compatible with Python 3.10, and is forward compatible with PyTorch 1.12 which will be compatible with Python 3.10.  It looks like PyTorch [only checks the min python version](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/setup.py#L212), and doesn't check the max version.  I believe the right solution here is to file a PyTorch issue requesting they check both min and max Python versions.
